solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Symbolic figure’s unorthodox view of catechism (9)

indicatorNotes.unorthodox view of: an unorthodox view takes the word out of its usual order

annotation.surface: A religious symbol is presented as a heretic's odd reading of the catechism.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. SCHEMATIC is here a noun: a diagram, a figure standing for something.
annotation.definitionFit: A schematic is a symbolic diagram, a figure that represents something rather than depicting it.

entries.clue: Jumble sale involving divorced king and doctor (8)

indicatorNotes.involving: the sale takes the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.divorced: the king and the doctor are separated, going into the sale at two different points

blocks.note: the outer word, split as S…A…LE
MB = Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

annotation.surface: A jumble sale is somehow involved with a divorced king and a doctor, like a tabloid scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jumble sale' is a British charity sale of second-hand goods, but here the phrase splits and 'Jumble' is the definition. 'Divorced' is what lets the two insertions land in different places.
annotation.definitionFit: To jumble is to scramble, mixing things up into disorder.

entries.clue: Victor’s killing spree’s beginning amid appalling chaos and destruction (5)

indicatorNotes.killing: Victor kills the S, removing it from the word
indicatorNotes.amid: V sits in the middle of the other letters
indicatorNotes.appalling: chaos is made appalling, i.e. rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder before the S goes
first letter of spree, the letter removed
V = Victor in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A man called Victor goes on a killing spree amid appalling chaos and destruction.
annotation.walkthrough: Victor both removes the S of CHAOS and then takes its place among the rearranged letters: HA(V)OC.
annotation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread destruction, as in 'wreak havoc'.

entries.clue: Harm witness curbing trouble in city (9)

indicatorNotes.curbing: SEE holds ILL in check, containing it

blocks.note: an ill = a trouble or misfortune

annotation.surface: Someone harms a witness in the course of stopping trouble in a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harm witness' reads like witness intimidation, but it splits into two verbs; the city is the French port.
annotation.definitionFit: Marseille is the great port city of southern France.

entries.clue: US writer and English writer bringing up god (7)

indicatorNotes.bringing up: in a down answer, the god is brought up to the top of the column

blocks.note: Thor, Norse god of thunder, lifted out of AUTHOR
E (English) + AUTHOR (writer), with THOR taken from its end and brought up to the top

annotation.surface: An American and an English writer between them raise a god, as if collaborating on myth.
annotation.walkthrough: The god is not an extra piece: he is already hiding at the end of AUTHOR, and 'bringing up' moves him to the top of the down answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau was the American writer of Walden.

entries.clue: Nurse resembling pop star? (7)

annotation.surface: A nurse is said to look like a pop star.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' is a verb here, as in nursing a hope; the wordplay reads backwards from the surface, pop star first, then -ish.
annotation.definitionFit: To nurse a hope or grudge is to cherish it, holding it dear.

entries.clue: Place to store valuables and money for those attending (5)

indicatorNotes.for those attending: those attending are an audience, who hear the word

blocks.note: cash = money, and the answer is spelt differently but said identically

annotation.surface: A safe for valuables and money, provided for the guests at some event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Those attending' means listeners: an audience attends to what it hears.
annotation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store, a place where valuables are kept.

entries.clue: Stuck-up title adopted by politically correct firm (5)

indicatorNotes.Stuck-up: in a down answer, stuck up means read from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.adopted by: PC takes SIR in, like a family adopting a child

annotation.surface: A snobbish title is taken on by a firm that is anxious to be politically correct.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but is the adjective; P(SIR)C is then turned upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: Crisp means firm and brittle, as a crisp apple is.

entries.clue: Business partnerships in contact with group hosted by government agency (9)

indicatorNotes.hosted by: the agency is the host, holding the other letters inside

blocks.note: a sort = a kind or group

annotation.surface: Companies in partnership deal with a group sheltered by a government agency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In contact with' gives ON, as a picture is on a wall, touching it.
annotation.definitionFit: Consortia is the plural of consortium, an association of businesses.

entries.clue: One by one represents this team (6)

annotation.definition: One by one represents this team

blocks.note: the surface means one after another; the setter means the digit 1 written beside another 1
the number so written is also the name for a side of that many players

annotation.surface: A team that is represented member by member.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One by one' suggests individually, but it means a 1 next to a 1: 11. A cricket or football side is called an eleven.
annotation.definitionFit: An eleven is a cricket or football team, and 11 is literally one by one.

entries.clue: Part of country’s liquid assets entirely controlled by banks? (5)

annotation.definition: Part of country’s liquid assets entirely controlled by banks?

blocks.note: the surface means a nation's cash; the setter means water running through its land
the surface means financial banks; the setter means the grassy edges that hold the water in

annotation.surface: A nation's cash reserves are wholly in the hands of the banks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is finance: liquid assets and banks. Read literally, the liquid is water and the banks are riverbanks.
annotation.definitionFit: A river is a stretch of a country's water held between its banks.

entries.clue: Live and die whenever nurses following rules (9)

indicatorNotes.nurses: ONCE holds the other letters, as a nurse holds a baby

annotation.surface: Advice to live, die and care for people always by the rules, like a nun's vow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like people in the surface but holds the other words, and 'whenever' giving ONCE is the stretch to spot.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: obedience is conduct that keeps to the rules one is given.

entries.clue: Ship’s officer commandeers revolutionary cutter (7)

indicatorNotes.commandeers: the mate seizes the revolutionary, taking him inside

blocks.note: a mate is a ship's officer

annotation.surface: A ship's mate seizes a rebel's boat, a cutter being a kind of vessel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' sits well with ships, where it is a small vessel; here it is anything that cuts, and the revolutionary is the stock crossword Che Guevara.
annotation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife, a cutter for clearing vegetation.

entries.clue: Urchin learning to beg (7)

blocks.note: an imp = a mischievous child, an urchin

annotation.surface: A street child picks up the art of begging.
annotation.walkthrough: IMP is a stock crossword urchin: a mischievous child rather than a demon.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with implore carrying extra urgency and desperation beyond a simple request.

entries.clue: Governing body’s pub expert (5,9)

blocks.note: your local is your nearest pub

annotation.surface: A council keeps its own specialist on pubs.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the neighbourhood pub one regularly drinks at. A local authority is a British council running a town or county.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in British usage: the council that runs a town or county is its governing body.

entries.clue: City bearing daily effect of The Sun’s fraud (9)

indicatorNotes.bearing: in a down answer, LA bears CHAR, carrying it on top

blocks.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day

annotation.surface: A city paper exposes The Sun, a British tabloid, as a fraud with daily consequences.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Daily' and 'The Sun' suggest newspapers, but a daily is a cleaner and the sun is the real one in the sky.
annotation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud who claims skills he doesn't have.

entries.clue: Company’s practice again tries case on approval (9)

indicatorNotes.case: the case of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

blocks.note: a court hears, or tries, a case

annotation.surface: A firm's legal practice retries a case that is on approval.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Company' and 'practice' sound like business, and 'tries case' like a court; the company is a theatre company. RE-HEARS is tries again.
annotation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a theatre company's practice run of a play.

entries.clue: American child celebrity making a comeback in concert (2,3,3)

indicatorNotes.making a comeback: the celebrity comes back, i.e. is written backwards

blocks.note: a big name is a celebrity

annotation.surface: A US child star makes a comeback in a live concert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In concert' looks like a music venue but means acting together.
annotation.definitionFit: To act as one man is to act all together, in concert.

entries.clue: Exploit quite different things, as side-splitting witticisms do? (4,2,4,4)

blocks.note: the idiom for exploiting two contrary positions at once
splitting and witticisms each contain IT forwards and TI backwards

annotation.surface: A comedian's hilarious one-liners serve two purposes at once.
annotation.walkthrough: Side-splitting suggests belly laughs, but look at the words: splITTIng and wITTIcisms each hold IT one way and then the other.
annotation.definitionFit: Having it both ways means enjoying the benefits of two incompatible things.

entries.clue: Outside broadcast short of electricity? (7)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are strewn about

annotation.surface: An outside broadcast loses its power supply.
annotation.walkthrough: An outside broadcast is a TV transmission from a location. The definition is figurative: electricity as excitement, so lacking it is dull.
annotation.definitionFit: Something tedious lacks electricity in the sense of any spark or excitement.

entries.clue: Means of communicating acceptable system of logical rules (7)

blocks.note: an organ = a newspaper or journal, a medium of communication

annotation.surface: A communication method that is fine as a logical framework.
annotation.walkthrough: The Organon is the name for Aristotle's works on logic; the word is used generally for any system of reasoning.
annotation.definitionFit: An organon is a system of rules for scientific or philosophical reasoning.

entries.clue: New version of atlas contains listing (6)

indicatorNotes.version of: a new version of the word is its letters rewritten
indicatorNotes.contains: the rearranged atlas holds N inside

annotation.surface: A new edition of an atlas contains a gazetteer listing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Listing' is not a list here but a ship's lean. ASLA(N)T.
annotation.definitionFit: Listing means leaning to one side, which is what aslant means.

entries.clue: Married disciple’s not one to stray (7)

indicatorNotes.not: not one: the I is taken away
indicatorNotes.to stray: the remaining letters wander out of order

annotation.surface: A married follower of some faith is not one to be unfaithful.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is'. 'Spliced' is informal British for married, from joining two ropes.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang, from splicing two ropes together: to be spliced is to be joined in marriage.

entries.clue: Who minds relinquishing fourth place in race? (5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Who minds' stands for 'one who minds', a noun

indicatorNotes.relinquishing: the word gives up a letter

annotation.surface: A question about who cares if a runner gives up fourth place in a race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Race' is a verb: to career is to rush headlong. 'Minds' means looks after.
annotation.definitionFit: A carer is someone who minds, or looks after, another person.

entries.clue: Cheer up good boy with depression briefly (7)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short: the last letter goes

annotation.surface: Advice to cheer up a good boy who is feeling low for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low spirits but is a dent, a hollow.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gladden means to make glad, lifting someone's spirits.

entries.clue: I’m annoyed about female personnel in the military (5)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the exclamation wraps itself round the female

annotation.surface: Someone is irritated about the women serving in the armed forces.
annotation.walkthrough: The draft is American usage for conscripts, the people called up to serve.
annotation.definitionFit: A draft is a body of personnel selected for military service.

entries.clue: PM next in importance to almost nobody (9)

indicatorNotes.almost: the word is not quite complete: the last letter goes

blocks.note: after = second to, as in 'after him, she is most important'
NO ONE without its last letter

annotation.surface: The Prime Minister is second in importance to almost nobody.
annotation.walkthrough: PM reads as Prime Minister in a surface about importance, but it is post meridiem, the afternoon.
annotation.definitionFit: p.m. marks the hours after noon, the afternoon.

entries.clue: Non-commissioned officer charged with fighting migrants from colony (5)

indicatorNotes.charged with: the officer is loaded with fighting, which fills him

annotation.surface: A sergeant is accused of attacking people who have left a colony.
annotation.walkthrough: The colony is of bees, not a country; a swarm leaves the hive to found a new one.
annotation.definitionFit: A swarm is a mass of bees migrating from their colony.

entries.clue: Singer in Blur one talked about (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer lies inside the next words

annotation.surface: A member of the band Blur is being gossiped about.
annotation.walkthrough: Blur is a British rock band, which makes the words look like a music-news snippet; 'talked about' sounds like a homophone but 'about' reverses.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice.

entries.clue: Underwear worn by bachelor? (9)

blocks.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest

annotation.surface: An undershirt worn by an unmarried man.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: a bachelor is one kind of singleton.
annotation.definitionFit: A singleton is a person who is not in a relationship, like a bachelor.
